clarifications: Are there duplicate prerequisites? No, each prerequisite pair is unique.
Can there be a course with no prerequisites? Yes, some courses may not require any other courses.
What should be returned if there are no prerequisites? Return true, as all courses can be finished.
Are self-dependencies allowed? No, a course cannot be a prerequisite of itself.
Is the input always valid? Yes, the input will always adhere to the constraints.
What if numCourses is 1? Return true, as the single course can be completed.
Can the prerequisites list be empty? Yes, it can be empty, which means no course has prerequisites.
expectedApproaches: Topological Sort using Kahn's Algorithm with O(V + E) time complexity.
Depth First Search (DFS) to detect cycles with O(V + E) time complexity.
solutions: Use Kahn's Algorithm for topological sorting: Initialize an in-degree array for each course. Traverse the prerequisites to fill the in-degree array. Use a queue to collect courses with zero in-degree. Process the queue, reducing in-degrees of dependent courses and adding new zero in-degree courses to the queue. If all courses are processed, return true; otherwise, return false.

Use Depth First Search (DFS) to detect cycles: Create an adjacency list for the graph. Track visited nodes with three states: unvisited, visiting, and visited. For each unvisited course, perform a DFS. If a cycle is detected during DFS, return false. If all courses are processed without finding a cycle, return true.
commonMistakes: Not checking for cycles in the graph.
Incorrectly updating in-degrees in Kahn's Algorithm.
Failing to mark nodes as visited in DFS, leading to infinite loops.
Assuming all courses must have prerequisites.
